faq.answerKey: Venus Protocol is a trusted decentralized finance lending and borrowing protocol that's deployed on the BNB Chain. it combines the stablecoin minting facility of Maker and the algorithmic money markets developed by Compound, providing a simplified user experience and core capabilities in a single application.

XVS is the governance token for the Venus protocol. By supplying certain tokens, you can earn XVS from the protocols as extra rewards on top of base interest. XVS token holders can also propose and vote on changes to the Venus protocol.

faq.titleKey: How does the staking mechanism work in Venus Protocol?
faq.answerKey: Venus allows users to stake various assets, including stablecoins, core pool assets (like BTCB, ETH, TRX), and XVS. Users can provide liquidity to these pools and earn interest. Users can withdraw funds on demand or receive Venus Tokens (vTokens) representing your stake. vTokens are as freely tradable as any other cryptographic asset on BNB Chain.

faq.titleKey: What risks should I be aware of when borrowing from Venus Protocol?
faq.answerKey: When borrowing from Venus, you should be aware of risks such as liquidation risk if your collateral value falls below the required threshold, and interest rate fluctuations that can increase your borrowing costs.

faq.titleKey: How are interest rates calculated for borrowed assets on Venus?
faq.answerKey: Interest rates on Venus are algorithmically determined based on supply and demand dynamics for each asset. When demand to borrow an asset increases, the interest rate rises, and vice versa. The loan interest is calculated per block and compounded into your borrow balance. Therefore, the “Token borrowed” balance under "Overall position" reflects your total borrowed plus the accrued interest.

evidence.description: Lista DAO is a decentralized stablecoin lending protocol powered by LSDfi. Users can undergo staking and liquid staking on Lista, as well as borrow lisUSD against a variety of decentralized collateral. Lista aims to position lisUSD as the number one stablecoin in the crypto space, leveraging on innovative liquid staking solutions.

faq.answerKey: Lista DAO functions as the open-source decentralized stablecoin lending protocol powered by LSDfi.

slisBNB is the native yield bearing and liquid staking token for BNB, built by Lista DAO. slisBNB appreciates against BNB in line with BNB’s staking APR, allowing users have the freedom to earn additional yields on different DeFi platforms while earning staking rewards passively.

faq.titleKey: What is the minimum BNB I can stake?
faq.answerKey: The minimum stake value is 0.0001 BNB.

Lista Lending is a permissionless lending protocol built on isolated market architecture. Each market consists of one collateral asset and one loan asset, operating independently. Risk is not shared between markets. Borrowers deposit collateral and borrow against it. Each market has its own LLTV (Liquidation Loan-to-Value) ratio, interest rate, and liquidity depth.

At Lista Lending, interest rate is determined by our Interest Rate Model (IRM) based on the supply and demand of the loan asset. The key indicator of the supply and demand is market utilization rate - the ratio between borrowed and supplied assets.

Each Lista market has a Liquidation Loan-To-Value (LLTV) threshold. If your LTV exceeds the LLTV, either because your collateral value drops or your debt grows from accrued interest, your position becomes eligible for liquidation. To stay safe, keep your LTV well below the LLTV and top up collateral or repay early if the market moves against you.

checks.title: Run by someone other than the listed protocol
checks.detail: The listing says Lista. The contract calls itself "RockawayX PT Yield" (roxptUSDT). That is the pattern of a curated vault, where the listing names the lending protocol and the contract names the curator who actually sets the risk policy. Your money answers to the second one, and the listing never mentions them.

consequence.brief: RockawayX PT Yield decides what your money is lent against, not Lista.
consequence.full: Your deposit does not sit still. It is lent out, and someone decides what it may be lent against, at what ratio, and priced by which oracle. Here that someone is the curator, not Lista. If those limits are set loosely and borrowers default while their collateral is falling, the vault takes the loss and your deposit does not come back whole. Any score or reputation you are relying on belongs to Lista, and does not cover the curator's decisions.

checks.title: Code can be replaced
checks.detail: 0xb5a30e1fa2cf3c8dea882124b3ab5a47a27c5dd2 forwards to 0x713a7e23cff5016a479b079e48b575818a3fcc95, and that target can be changed. What was confirmed above is what runs today, not necessarily what runs when the money comes back out.

consequence.brief: One keyholder can swap the code holding your money, without warning.
consequence.full: Whoever holds that key can swap the code holding your money, without asking and without warning, including for code that moves it somewhere else. Nothing here says they will. It says your deposit is protected by trust in that keyholder rather than by the code just verified, and that this is the mechanism behind several of the largest losses in DeFi.
